title: Infection Spread Simulation IV — Transition Death
prompt:
This is the fourth level of a staged grid-infection exercise. Use `HEALTHY = 0`, `INFECTED = 1`, `IMMUNE = 2`, and `DEAD = 3`.

Implement `simulate_transition_death(grid, infectious_days, death_threshold, infection_threshold=2, directions=DIR4)`. An infected cell transmits for exactly `infectious_days` daily updates. Each day is synchronous and uses the start-of-day grid and active-infection ages:
- A healthy cell becomes infected when it has at least `infection_threshold` active infected neighbors. A newly infected cell gets the full timer and cannot decrement or transmit until a later day.
- An initially immune cell and any cell that becomes immune never changes or transmits.
- When an existing infected cell finishes its final infectious day, examine its number of active infected neighbors in the start-of-day snapshot. It becomes `DEAD` when that number is at least `death_threshold`; otherwise it becomes `IMMUNE`. Dead cells never change or transmit.

Return `(days_to_no_active_infections, final_grid)`. The day on which an infected cell transitions still counts as an infectious day. Do not mutate the input grid. You may assume a non-empty rectangular grid, valid state values, and positive thresholds/timers.
